Yuitility is a local-first platform designed to run completely inside your browser's sandboxed memory. File compression, syntax conversions, and PDF formatting execute locally on your CPU - meaning zero network uploads, zero latency, and absolute file safety. Our pillars of local execution. Yuitility was created as an alternative to utility websites filled with trackers, pop-up ads, and server processing queues. We run on three design principles. 01 Client CPU Isolation Calculations are run using local client-side engines. By performing conversions inside your browser memory, your files are protected from database breaches or leakages. 02 Zero Transmission We believe that the safest place for your private files, salary charts, and API tokens is on your own hard drive. Yuitility guarantees zero file uploads. 03 Clean Workspace No signups, subscription paywalls, or daily document limits. Yuitility is maintained as a fast, clean toolkit optimized for instant production usage. How it runs in browser. Traditional utility websites require an internet connection to send files to external cloud queues. Yuitility runs locally by compiling heavy backend scripts directly into browser bundles. WebAssembly Integration For CPU-intensive tasks like converting file formats, extracting archives, or rendering PDFs, we compile performant libraries into WASM. This allows binary execution inside the browser sandbox at near-native speeds. 2. Isolated JavaScript Subroutines Financial calculations, hash generation, and text formatting are evaluated in client-side JavaScript threads. These run inside your browser's V8 storage instance, isolated from other tabs and disconnected from network triggers. 3. Offline Web Application caching Yuitility is cacheable as a Progressive Web App (PWA). All assets and engine bundles are saved on your local device. Your confidential documents, financial figures, and passcodes remain strictly offline inside your device cache, immune to remote database leaks. Yuitility compiles the logic locally, delivering instant file conversions with zero latency. Is Yuitility completely free to use? Yes. mainEntity.name: How is EMI calculated?

acceptedAnswer.text: EMI = [P x R x (1+R)^N] / [(1+R)^N - 1], where P is the principal, R is the monthly interest rate, and N is the number of monthly installments.

mainEntity.name: Why does more interest get paid in the early months?

acceptedAnswer.text: In a reducing-balance loan, interest is calculated on the outstanding principal. Early on, the outstanding balance is highest, so a larger share of each EMI goes toward interest rather than principal.

mainEntity.name: Does prepayment reduce my EMI or my tenure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Depends on the lender's policy - some reduce your tenure while keeping EMI the same, others reduce your EMI while keeping tenure the same. Check with your lender which option applies.

mainEntity.name: Is a lower EMI always better?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily - a lower EMI usually means a longer tenure, which increases total interest paid over the life of the loan.

The formula EMI = P × r × (1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1) · P — principal, the amount actually borrowed (after down payment, before fees) · r — interest rate per month = annual rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100 · n — tenure in months Worked example A ₹50,00,000 home loan at 8.5% for 20 years. r (monthly rate) 8.5 ÷ 12 ÷ 100 = 0.0070833 n (months) 20 × 12 = 240 (1 + r)ⁿ 1.0070833²⁴⁰ = 5.44127 EMI 5000000 × 0.0070833 × 5.44127 ÷ 4.44127 EMI = ₹43,391 per month. Total repaid ₹1,04,13,879, of which ₹54,13,879 is interest — more than the amount borrowed. In month 1 of that loan, ₹35,417 of the ₹43,391 payment is interest and only ₹7,975 reduces the principal — 18% of your payment. That ratio is why prepaying early is worth far more than prepaying late. Where this calculation usually goes wrong Comparing EMIs instead of total interest A longer tenure always produces a smaller, more attractive EMI. On the ₹8,00,000 car loan at 9.5% above, stretching 60 months to 84 months drops the EMI from ₹16,801 to ₹13,075 — and raises total interest from ₹2,08,089 to ₹2,98,316. You pay ₹90,000 for the comfort of a smaller number. Using the sanctioned amount as the principal Processing fees, insurance bundled into the loan and GST on those fees are often deducted from disbursal but charged interest on. Use the amount credited plus anything financed, not the headline sanction. Assuming the rate is fixed Most floating-rate loans reprice against a benchmark. When the rate moves, lenders usually hold the EMI constant and change the tenure instead, so the loan quietly gets longer rather than more expensive per month. Edge cases worth knowing Zero interest rate The standard formula divides by ((1+r)ⁿ − 1), which is zero when r = 0. At 0% the EMI is simply P ÷ n. This calculator handles that case rather than returning an error or infinity. Part-prepayment A lump-sum prepayment reduces principal immediately. You then choose to keep the EMI (tenure shortens, maximum interest saved) or reduce the EMI (tenure unchanged, less saved). Keeping the EMI is almost always the cheaper option. How is EMI calculated? EMI = [P x R x (1+R)^N] / [(1+R)^N - 1], where P is the principal, R is the monthly interest rate, and N is the number of monthly installments. Why does more interest get paid in the early months? In a reducing-balance loan, interest is calculated on the outstanding principal. Early on, the outstanding balance is highest, so a larger share of each EMI goes toward interest rather than principal. Does prepayment reduce my EMI or my tenure? Depends on the lender's policy - some reduce your tenure while keeping EMI the same, others reduce your EMI while keeping tenure the same. Check with your lender which option applies. Is a lower EMI always better? Not necessarily - a lower EMI usually means a longer tenure, which increases total interest paid over the life of the loan. mainEntity.name: What is a SIP?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Systematic Investment Plan lets you invest a fixed amount regularly (usually monthly) into a mutual fund, rather than investing a lump sum at once.

mainEntity.name: How accurate are SIP return projections?

acceptedAnswer.text: Projections use an assumed constant annual return rate for simplicity, but actual mutual fund returns fluctuate year to year. Treat projections as an estimate, not a guarantee.

mainEntity.name: Does SIP investing average out market volatility?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - this is called rupee-cost averaging. Investing a fixed amount regularly means you buy more units when prices are low and fewer when prices are high, which can smooth out volatility over time.

mainEntity.name: Why does the corpus grow faster in later years?

acceptedAnswer.text: Compounding accelerates over time as returns are generated on both your contributions and previously accumulated returns, so the growth curve is not linear.

acceptedAnswer.text: The calculator computes elapsed time calendar-day by calendar-day using exact calendar rules. For leap years, February 29 is factored into day counts accurately without rough 30-day or 365-day approximations.

mainEntity.name: Does the calculation account for time zones or exact birth times?

acceptedAnswer.text: The live seconds counter runs against your local browser clock and the selected birth date/time. If an exact birth time is omitted, standard midnight (00:00:00) is used as the starting boundary.

mainEntity.name: Is my birth date or personal data stored or transmitted?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Your birth date, zodiac signs, and countdown computations run 100% locally inside your browser memory. Nothing is sent to any server or recorded in a database.

mainEntity.name: Why might my age in days differ from multiplying years by 365?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiplying years by 365 ignores leap years (366 days) and the varying lengths of elapsed calendar months (28 to 31 days). Our engine calculates every discrete calendar day elapsed between the two dates.

mainEntity.name: Is length or complexity more important for password strength?

acceptedAnswer.text: Length generally matters more - a longer passphrase with moderate complexity is typically harder to crack than a short password stuffed with special characters.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to generate passwords online?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's safe if the generation happens entirely client-side (in your browser) rather than being sent to and generated on a server - check that the tool you're using works this way.

mainEntity.name: Should I use a different password for every account?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - reusing passwords means a breach on one site can compromise your accounts elsewhere. A password manager paired with generated unique passwords is the standard recommendation.

mainEntity.name: Does Yuitility store my generated passwords?

acceptedAnswer.text: Never. Passwords are generated in your local browser tab memory using Web Crypto API.

mainEntity.name: Is the "1 dog year = 7 human years" rule accurate?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. That rule is outdated. Dogs mature much faster in their first two years, then aging slows down - and the rate varies significantly by size. Small dogs (under 20 lbs) age slower in later years; large and giant breeds age faster.

mainEntity.name: Does dog breed affect the calculation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, significantly. A 10-year-old Chihuahua and a 10-year-old Great Dane are at very different life stages. Larger breeds generally have shorter lifespans and hit "senior" status earlier.

mainEntity.name: At what age is a dog considered a senior?

acceptedAnswer.text: Small breeds are typically senior around 10-12 years old, medium breeds around 8-10, and large/giant breeds as early as 6-7 years old.

mainEntity.name: How accurate is this calculator?

acceptedAnswer.text: It uses current veterinary research-based formulas rather than the old linear multiplier, giving a much closer approximation of your dog's biological age. Individual health and genetics still play a role.

mainEntity.name: Which clinical formula is used to calculate the estimated due date (EDD)?

acceptedAnswer.text: The calculation applies Naegele's rule (adding 280 days or 40 weeks to the first day of your Last Menstrual Period) assuming an average 28-day menstrual cycle. If conception date is selected, 266 days are added.

mainEntity.name: How accurate is the estimated due date?

acceptedAnswer.text: An estimated due date is a clinical benchmark: only about 4-5% of babies are born on their exact due date, while roughly 80% arrive within two weeks before or after. Clinical ultrasound dating performed by your obstetrician remains the standard.

mainEntity.name: Does this pregnancy calculator provide medical diagnosis or replace obstetric care?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This tool is designed strictly for personal gestational tracking and milestone planning. Always consult your obstetrician, certified midwife, or healthcare provider for medical evaluation and clinical dating scans.

mainEntity.name: Why does inflation matter so much in retirement planning?

acceptedAnswer.text: Over 20-30 years, even moderate inflation significantly erodes purchasing power - expenses that feel comfortable today will cost substantially more by the time you retire, so plans need to account for this.

mainEntity.name: How is the required corpus calculated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Generally by estimating your annual post-retirement expenses (inflation-adjusted) and calculating the lump sum needed to sustain those withdrawals for your expected retirement duration, accounting for continued investment growth.

mainEntity.name: What return rate should I assume?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends on your investment mix - conservative (largely debt) portfolios might assume 6-8%, while equity-heavy portfolios might assume higher long-term averages, though actual returns vary and are never guaranteed.

mainEntity.name: Is my retirement goal stored anywhere?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. All projections execute locally in your browser memory with zero server tracking.

The maths behind the retirement age & fund calculator So you can check the result rather than take it on trust. The formula Future monthly need = current monthly need × (1 + inflation)ⁿ · n — years until retirement · The corpus is then sized against that future need, not today's Worked example ₹50,000 of monthly expenses today, retiring in 25 years, assuming 6% inflation. Inflation factor 1.06²⁵ = 4.2919 Monthly need at retirement 50,000 × 4.2919 = ₹2,14,594 Annual need at retirement ₹25,75,122 At a 4% safe withdrawal rate, that implies a corpus of roughly ₹6,43,78,000. Almost every under-saving story starts here: people size the corpus against today's ₹50,000 and arrive at about ₹1.5 crore. Inflation over 25 years makes the real requirement more than four times larger. The number that feels absurd is usually the correct one. Where this calculation usually goes wrong Healthcare inflation is not general inflation Medical costs have historically risen faster than the headline rate, and they rise exactly when you are retired. Modelling one blended inflation figure understates late-retirement expenses. Retirement is not the end date The corpus has to survive a retirement that may last 25–30 years, so it must keep growing after you stop contributing. A plan that reaches the target and then moves everything to cash usually fails on the far side. Why does inflation matter so much in retirement planning? Over 20-30 years, even moderate inflation significantly erodes purchasing power - expenses that feel comfortable today will cost substantially more by the time you retire, so plans need to account for this. How is the required corpus calculated? Generally by estimating your annual post-retirement expenses (inflation-adjusted) and calculating the lump sum needed to sustain those withdrawals for your expected retirement duration, accounting for continued investment growth. What return rate should I assume? This depends on your investment mix - conservative (largely debt) portfolios might assume 6-8%, while equity-heavy portfolios might assume higher long-term averages, though actual returns vary and are never guaranteed. acceptedAnswer.text: Generally: below 18.5 is underweight, 18.5-24.9 is normal weight, 25-29.9 is overweight, and 30+ is considered obese, though these thresholds are population-level guidelines, not individual diagnoses.

mainEntity.name: What other measures complement BMI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Waist circumference, body fat percentage, and waist-to-hip ratio are commonly used alongside BMI for a fuller picture of health risk.

mainEntity.name: What is a moratorium period in an education loan?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's the period during your course (plus usually 6-12 months after) when you're not required to make EMI payments. Interest still accrues during this time and is typically added to your principal - this calculator factors that in.

mainEntity.name: Can I claim tax benefits on education loan interest?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in India, interest paid on education loans qualifies for a deduction under Section 80E, with no upper limit on the deduction amount, for up to 8 years or until the interest is fully repaid.

mainEntity.name: Should I pay interest during the moratorium period if I can afford it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Paying interest during the moratorium (simple interest, before it compounds into principal) can reduce your total loan cost significantly - many lenders offer a discount for this.

mainEntity.name: How is the EMI calculated after the moratorium ends?

acceptedAnswer.text: The accrued interest during the moratorium is added to the principal, and EMIs are then calculated on this new (higher) principal amount over the remaining tenure.

The maths behind the bike & two-wheeler loan emi calculator So you can check the result rather than take it on trust. The formula EMI = P × r × (1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1) · P — on-road price minus down payment · r — annual rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100 · n — tenure in months Worked example ₹1,50,000 on-road, ₹30,000 down payment, 11% for 3 years. mainEntity.name: How often does bank FD interest compound?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most Indian banks compound FD interest quarterly, though this varies - check your specific bank's terms, since monthly vs quarterly compounding changes your maturity value.

mainEntity.name: Is FD interest taxable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in India, FD interest is added to your taxable income and taxed at your applicable slab rate, with TDS deducted by the bank if interest exceeds the threshold.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between cumulative and non-cumulative FDs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cumulative FDs reinvest interest and pay out the full amount at maturity; non-cumulative FDs pay interest periodically (monthly/quarterly) as income instead.

mainEntity.name: Can I use this FD calculator for NRE/NRO fixed deposits?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it works for standard resident FDs as well as NRE and NRO fixed deposits.

mainEntity.name: Does the time period need to be in years?

acceptedAnswer.text: The formula works with any consistent time unit as long as the interest rate matches that unit - most commonly expressed as an annual rate with time in years.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. All simple interest calculations run 100% locally in browser memory.

mainEntity.name: How is PPF interest calculated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Interest is compounded annually but calculated monthly based on the lowest balance in your account between the 5th and last day of each month.

mainEntity.name: Why does depositing before the 5th of the month matter?

acceptedAnswer.text: Since interest is calculated on the lowest balance between the 5th and month-end, depositing before the 5th ensures that month's contribution earns interest starting that same month, rather than missing out.

mainEntity.name: Is PPF interest and maturity amount taxable?

acceptedAnswer.text: No - PPF falls under the EEE (Exempt-Exempt-Exempt) tax category in India, meaning contributions, interest earned, and maturity proceeds are all tax-free, subject to applicable limits.

mainEntity.name: What is the maximum investment limit in PPF per year?

acceptedAnswer.text: The maximum contribution allowed in a PPF account is ₹1.5 lakh per financial year.

The maths behind the gold loan emi calculator So you can check the result rather than take it on trust. The formula EMI = P × r × (1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1) · P — loan amount sanctioned against the pledged gold · r — annual rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100 · n — tenure in months Worked example ₹3,00,000 gold loan at 9% for 24 months, repaid as a regular EMI. r 9 ÷ 12 ÷ 100 = 0.0075 n 24 (1 + r)²⁴ 1.19641 EMI = ₹13,705, total interest ₹28,930. Gold loans are frequently offered as bullet repayment (interest serviced monthly, principal at maturity) rather than EMI. Under bullet repayment on the same loan you would pay ₹2,250/month in interest and ₹3,00,000 at the end — a very different cash-flow shape for a similar total cost. Where this calculation usually goes wrong The loan is against value, not weight The sanctioned amount is a percentage of the assessed value of the gold content, so making charges, stones and the purity of the ornament all reduce what you can borrow against a given gram weight. The maths behind the hra exemption calculator So you can check the result rather than take it on trust. The formula Exempt HRA = the least of three amounts · 1. Actual HRA received from the employer · 2. Rent actually paid − 10% of basic salary (+ DA) · 3. 50% of basic salary for a metro city, 40% otherwise Worked example Basic salary ₹6,00,000, HRA received ₹3,00,000, rent paid ₹2,40,000 (₹20,000/month), metro city. Limb 1 — HRA received ₹3,00,000 Limb 2 — rent − 10% of basic 2,40,000 − 60,000 = ₹1,80,000 Limb 3 — 50% of basic ₹3,00,000 Exempt = ₹1,80,000 (limb 2 binds). Taxable HRA = ₹3,00,000 − ₹1,80,000 = ₹1,20,000. The binding limb is almost never the one people assume. Here it is rent, not the 50% metro cap — meaning a higher HRA component in the offer letter would have bought no extra exemption at all at this rent level. Where this calculation usually goes wrong The 10% subtraction is easy to forget Limb 2 is rent paid minus 10% of basic, not rent paid. Omitting the subtraction overstates the exemption by ₹60,000 in the example above. Observe: 0 outgoing requests are sent to any remote server. The maths behind the bmr calculator So you can check the result rather than take it on trust. The formula Mifflin-St Jeor: BMR = 10 × weight(kg) + 6.25 × height(cm) − 5 × age + s · s = +5 for men, −161 for women · TDEE = BMR × activity multiplier (1.2 sedentary to 1.9 very active) Worked example A 30-year-old man, 80 kg, 178 cm. 10 × weight 800 6.25 × height 1112.5 − 5 × age −150 + s +5 BMR = 1,767.5 kcal/day. At a 1.55 (moderate) multiplier, TDEE ≈ 2,740 kcal/day. The activity multiplier is the least reliable part of the calculation and the part with the largest effect: moving from 1.2 to 1.55 adds over 600 kcal to the daily target. Most people overestimate their activity level, which is why calculated targets often fail to produce the expected result. mainEntity.name: How do I open an MD file without installing special software?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can open any .md file directly in your web browser by dragging and dropping it onto this page or clicking 'Open .md File'. Our in-browser file reader parses and renders the Markdown text into formatted HTML with styled headings, tables, and code blocks instantly without needing VS Code, Obsidian, or desktop apps.

mainEntity.name: How do I convert or export Markdown (.md) to PDF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Click the 'MD to PDF' button in the live preview toolbar. This opens your operating system's native print engine with print-optimized CSS that removes UI buttons, centers the typography, and renders headers, tables, and code blocks cleanly into a downloadable PDF document.

mainEntity.name: Can I convert Markdown to Microsoft Word (.doc)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Click the 'MD to Word' button to generate an immediate .doc file containing all parsed headings, tables, and formatted lists. You can open and edit this file directly in Microsoft Word, Google Docs, or LibreOffice.

mainEntity.name: Which markdown formats and GitHub extensions are supported?

acceptedAnswer.text: The viewer supports full GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) including headings (H1-H6), bold, italic, strikethrough, blockquotes, GitHub callout alerts (> [!NOTE], > [!TIP], > [!WARNING]), aligned data tables, interactive task checklists (- [x]), and syntax-highlighted code fences.

mainEntity.name: Is my markdown file uploaded to any remote server?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The entire parsing and rendering process executes 100% locally in your web browser RAM using the HTML5 FileReader API. Your document content, filenames, and text never leave your computer or touch any external server.

acceptedAnswer.text: A calorie deficit occurs when you consume fewer calories than your body burns (TDEE), forcing your body to burn stored fat for energy.

mainEntity.name: What is a healthy daily calorie deficit?

acceptedAnswer.text: A deficit of 300 to 500 calories per day is recommended for safe, sustainable fat loss of approximately 0.5 to 1 lb per week.

mainEntity.name: How is TDEE calculated?

acceptedAnswer.text: TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure) is calculated using the Mifflin-St Jeor formula for BMR multiplied by your physical activity factor.

mainEntity.name: What is the official VTU formula to convert CGPA to percentage?

acceptedAnswer.text: The official VTU formula is Percentage = (CGPA - 0.75) * 10. For example, if your VTU CGPA is 8.20, your percentage is (8.20 - 0.75) * 10 = 74.50%.

mainEntity.name: Which VTU schemes use the (CGPA - 0.75) * 10 formula?

acceptedAnswer.text: This formula applies to VTU 2015, 2017, 2018, and CBCS schemes across B.E, B.Tech, M.Tech, and MCA programs under Visvesvaraya Technological University.

mainEntity.name: What is First Class with Distinction in VTU?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under VTU regulations, a CGPA of 7.75 and above (70.0% or higher) earned in the first attempt qualifies for First Class with Distinction.

The maths behind the home loan emi calculator So you can check the result rather than take it on trust. The formula EMI = P × r × (1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1) · P — Home loan principal (Sanctioned amount − down payment, typically 80% to 90% LTV) · r — Monthly interest rate = Annual interest rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100 · n — Loan tenure in months (up to 360 months for 30-year mortgages) Worked example A ₹75,00,000 home loan at 8.75% for 25 years. r (monthly rate) 8.75 ÷ 12 ÷ 100 = 0.0072917 n (months) 25 × 12 = 300 (1 + r)³⁰⁰ 1.0072917³⁰⁰ = 8.8131 Monthly EMI 7500000 × 0.0072917 × 8.8131 ÷ 7.8131 EMI = ₹61,659 per month. Total repaid ₹1,84,97,643, of which ₹1,09,97,643 is interest. Over 25 years at 8.75%, the interest paid (₹1.10 Crore) is 1.46 times the amount borrowed. Prepaying even ₹5,000 extra per month cuts your repayment tenure by over 4 years and saves over ₹22 Lakhs in net interest. Where this calculation usually goes wrong Ignoring the Repo Linked Lending Rate (RLLR) resets All floating rate home loans in India are pegged to the RBI Repo Rate. When the RBI raises or cuts the repo rate, your interest rate and tenure adjust automatically. Missing tax deductions under Section 24(b) and Section 80C Under the Old Tax Regime, interest up to ₹2 Lakh/year is deductible under Section 24(b), and principal up to ₹1.5 Lakh under Section 80C. Under the New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC), self-occupied home loan deductions are disallowed. At 8.5% interest, the monthly EMI for a ₹30 Lakh home loan for 20 years is ₹26,035. Total interest paid over 20 years is ₹32,48,328. The maths behind the home loan emi calculator So you can check the result rather than take it on trust. The formula EMI = P × r × (1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1) · P — Home loan principal (Sanctioned amount − down payment, typically 80% to 90% LTV) · r — Monthly interest rate = Annual interest rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100 · n — Loan tenure in months (up to 360 months for 30-year mortgages) Worked example A ₹75,00,000 home loan at 8.75% for 25 years. r (monthly rate) 8.75 ÷ 12 ÷ 100 = 0.0072917 n (months) 25 × 12 = 300 (1 + r)³⁰⁰ 1.0072917³⁰⁰ = 8.8131 Monthly EMI 7500000 × 0.0072917 × 8.8131 ÷ 7.8131 EMI = ₹61,659 per month. Total repaid ₹1,84,97,643, of which ₹1,09,97,643 is interest. Over 25 years at 8.75%, the interest paid (₹1.10 Crore) is 1.46 times the amount borrowed. Prepaying even ₹5,000 extra per month cuts your repayment tenure by over 4 years and saves over ₹22 Lakhs in net interest. Where this calculation usually goes wrong Ignoring the Repo Linked Lending Rate (RLLR) resets All floating rate home loans in India are pegged to the RBI Repo Rate. When the RBI raises or cuts the repo rate, your interest rate and tenure adjust automatically. Missing tax deductions under Section 24(b) and Section 80C Under the Old Tax Regime, interest up to ₹2 Lakh/year is deductible under Section 24(b), and principal up to ₹1.5 Lakh under Section 80C. Under the New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC), self-occupied home loan deductions are disallowed. Statutory Authorities & Official References Regulatory standards, published statutory gazettes, and official research governing this computation. The maths behind the home loan emi calculator So you can check the result rather than take it on trust. The formula EMI = P × r × (1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1) · P — Home loan principal (Sanctioned amount − down payment, typically 80% to 90% LTV) · r — Monthly interest rate = Annual interest rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100 · n — Loan tenure in months (up to 360 months for 30-year mortgages) Worked example A ₹75,00,000 home loan at 8.75% for 25 years. r (monthly rate) 8.75 ÷ 12 ÷ 100 = 0.0072917 n (months) 25 × 12 = 300 (1 + r)³⁰⁰ 1.0072917³⁰⁰ = 8.8131 Monthly EMI 7500000 × 0.0072917 × 8.8131 ÷ 7.8131 EMI = ₹61,659 per month. Total repaid ₹1,84,97,643, of which ₹1,09,97,643 is interest. Over 25 years at 8.75%, the interest paid (₹1.10 Crore) is 1.46 times the amount borrowed. Prepaying even ₹5,000 extra per month cuts your repayment tenure by over 4 years and saves over ₹22 Lakhs in net interest. Where this calculation usually goes wrong Ignoring the Repo Linked Lending Rate (RLLR) resets All floating rate home loans in India are pegged to the RBI Repo Rate. When the RBI raises or cuts the repo rate, your interest rate and tenure adjust automatically. Missing tax deductions under Section 24(b) and Section 80C Under the Old Tax Regime, interest up to ₹2 Lakh/year is deductible under Section 24(b), and principal up to ₹1.5 Lakh under Section 80C. Under the New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC), self-occupied home loan deductions are disallowed. The maths behind the salary in-hand calculator (india) So you can check the result rather than take it on trust. The formula Net In-Hand Salary = Gross CTC − (Employer EPF + Gratuity + Employer Insurance) − (Employee EPF + Professional Tax + Income Tax Deductions) · Gross Salary = Basic Pay + HRA + Special Allowance + Statutory Bonuses · Employee EPF = 12% of Basic Pay (capped or uncapped based on employer policy) · Professional Tax = Flat state slab (e.g. ₹200/month in Karnataka/Maharashtra) · Income Tax (TDS) = Monthly tax liability under New Regime (Sec 115BAC) or Old Regime Worked example Annual CTC of ₹15,00,000 under the New Tax Regime (FY 2025-26). If you have substantial deductions (80C, 80D, HRA, home loan interest), compare both regimes before filing your investment declarations. The maths behind the salary in-hand calculator (india) So you can check the result rather than take it on trust. The formula Net In-Hand Salary = Gross CTC − (Employer EPF + Gratuity + Employer Insurance) − (Employee EPF + Professional Tax + Income Tax Deductions) · Gross Salary = Basic Pay + HRA + Special Allowance + Statutory Bonuses · Employee EPF = 12% of Basic Pay (capped or uncapped based on employer policy) · Professional Tax = Flat state slab (e.g. ₹200/month in Karnataka/Maharashtra) · Income Tax (TDS) = Monthly tax liability under New Regime (Sec 115BAC) or Old Regime Worked example Annual CTC of ₹15,00,000 under the New Tax Regime (FY 2025-26). The maths behind the retirement age & fund calculator So you can check the result rather than take it on trust. The formula Future monthly need = current monthly need × (1 + inflation)ⁿ · n — years until retirement · The corpus is then sized against that future need, not today's Worked example ₹50,000 of monthly expenses today, retiring in 25 years, assuming 6% inflation. Inflation factor 1.06²⁵ = 4.2919 Monthly need at retirement 50,000 × 4.2919 = ₹2,14,594 Annual need at retirement ₹25,75,122 At a 4% safe withdrawal rate, that implies a corpus of roughly ₹6,43,78,000. Almost every under-saving story starts here: people size the corpus against today's ₹50,000 and arrive at about ₹1.5 crore. Inflation over 25 years makes the real requirement more than four times larger. The number that feels absurd is usually the correct one. Where this calculation usually goes wrong Healthcare inflation is not general inflation Medical costs have historically risen faster than the headline rate, and they rise exactly when you are retired. Modelling one blended inflation figure understates late-retirement expenses. Retirement is not the end date The corpus has to survive a retirement that may last 25–30 years, so it must keep growing after you stop contributing. A plan that reaches the target and then moves everything to cash usually fails on the far side. Visit Official Portal Frequently Asked Questions: 60-Month Auto Loan Payment Calculator What is the average monthly payment for a $35,000 car for 60 months? With $5,000 down payment and $3,000 trade-in ($27,000 loan amount) at 6.8% APR, the monthly payment is approximately $532. Total interest paid over 5 years is roughly $4,923. The maths behind the car loan emi calculator So you can check the result rather than take it on trust. The formula EMI = P × r × (1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1), where P = on-road price − down payment · On-road price includes ex-showroom price, registration, road tax and insurance · r — annual rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100 · n — tenure in months Worked example ₹10,00,000 on-road price, ₹2,00,000 down payment, 9.5% for 5 years. P (financed) 10,00,000 − 2,00,000 = 8,00,000 r 9.5 ÷ 12 ÷ 100 = 0.00791667 n 60 (1 + r)⁶⁰ 1.605068 EMI = ₹16,801. Total paid to the lender ₹10,08,089; interest ₹2,08,089. The car costs ₹10,00,000 but the transaction costs ₹12,08,089 once the down payment is included. Comparing that total against the car's value after five years is the honest version of the affordability question. Where this calculation usually goes wrong Financing the insurance and accessories Dealers routinely roll first-year insurance, extended warranty and accessories into the loan. These add to P and therefore attract interest for the full tenure — an ₹80,000 accessory package on a 5-year 9.5% loan costs about ₹1,01,000 by the end. Ignoring depreciation against the loan balance A car loses value faster in the first two years than a long loan repays principal. On a 7-year loan you can be several years in and still owe more than the car is worth, which matters if it is written off or you want to sell. Edge cases worth knowing Subvented / 'zero interest' schemes A 0% scheme usually carries a larger processing fee or a higher vehicle price. Compute the effective rate by comparing the total cash outflow against the cash-purchase price, not by trusting the advertised 0%. Making partial prepayments on your home loan is one of the most effective strategies to build long-term wealth. Because home loans use reducing-balance interest formulas, early payments directly reduce your principal balance, which in turn shrinks total interest accrued over the life of the loan. The Impact of Early Principal Prepayments When you start a 20-year or 30-year mortgage, the vast majority of your initial monthly payments go toward interest rather than principal reduction. By making an extra lump-sum payment or adding a small recurring amount each year, you bypass years of compounding interest. Accelerated Equity Building : You gain full ownership of your property much faster. Financial Freedom : Eliminating monthly debt obligations frees up cash flow for retirement investments or emergency buffers. Open Tool Now Developer & Text How to Convert JSON Data Arrays into Excel CSV Spreadsheets Quick Summary / TL;DR A step-by-step developer guide to converting JSON API arrays into clean CSV files for Excel analysis without uploading data to remote servers. JSON is the standard format for web APIs, database exports, and configuration files. However, business analysts, managers, and accountants often require tabular CSV files to perform spreadsheet formulas, pivot tables, and charts in Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets. Key Considerations When Converting JSON to CSV Array Structure : Your JSON input should be an array of uniform objects where each object key becomes a CSV column header. Nested Objects : Nested properties (such as user.address.city ) must be flattened into dot-notation column names. Delimiter Handling : Text strings containing commas or quotation marks must be escaped with double quotes to prevent column misalignment. How to Convert JSON to CSV in Browser Paste your JSON array into the [JSON to CSV Converter](/tools/json-to-csv-converter) on Yuitility. Weight loss fundamentally relies on energy balance. When you consume fewer calories than your body expends for daily physiological functions and physical movement, your body converts stored adipose tissue into energy. Understanding Key Metabolic Indicators Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) : The baseline number of calories your body burns at complete rest to maintain vital organs. Calculated using the Mifflin-St Jeor equation. Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE) : Your BMR multiplied by your physical activity multiplier (sedentary, moderate, or active lifestyle). Determining Your Safe Calorie Deficit Aggressive starvation diets often lead to muscle loss, metabolic slowing, and rapid weight regain. A moderate daily calorie deficit of 300 to 500 calories below your TDEE yields sustainable fat loss of approximately 0.5 to 1 pound per week. JSON Web Tokens (JWT) are widely used for client-server authentication in modern web applications. A standard JWT consists of three Base64URL-encoded strings separated by dots ( header.payload.signature ). Structure of a JWT Header : Defines the signing algorithm (such as RS256 or HS256) and token type. Payload (Claims) : Contains user identity data, permissions, issue timestamp ( iat ), and expiration timestamp ( exp ). Signature : Cryptographic hash validating token integrity. eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIiwibmFtZSI6IkFsaWNlIiwiaWF0IjoxNTE2MjM5MDIyfQ.SflKxwRJSMeKKF2QT4fwpMeJf36POk6yJV_adQssw5c Why Local JWT Decoding is Essential Pasting production authentication tokens into public cloud decoders can expose sensitive session keys, user IDs, and API authorizations. Using the [JWT Decoder](/tools/jwt-decoder) on Yuitility allows you to inspect payload claims and formatted dates locally in your browser memory. No tokens are sent over the network.
